author: GitHub
description:
What could be scarier at Halloween than your GitHub Actions credits running out? In this clip from the GitHub Podcast, Martin Woodward shows off his custom 3D-printed pumpkin powered by a microcontroller and addressable LEDs. The jack-o'-lantern monitors your live account quota, changing color as your credits drain and animating once they renew. Build your own spooky hardware alert by checking out the open-source code on GitHub.

author: GitHub
description:
AI tools can now generate clean, functional output from a short prompt, but the question is no longer how to write code; it is how to understand what has been made. In this GitHub Universe 2026 session, Qianqian Ye shows why sketching and thinking in code, beyond syntax, is essential when working with GitHub Copilot and open source tools like p5.js. Drawing from teaching creative coding at USC, Qianqian demonstrates how creative coding builds the intuition to shape systems, not just prompt them, and what is lost when that iterative process disappears. John Maeda connects the dots between design, computation, and the creative judgment that AI cannot replace

Speakers: 

John Maeda, CVP Engineering, GitHub Design and Microsoft CoreAI Design, Microsoft 
Qianqian Ye, Director of Creative Technology and Adjunct Associate Professor, Processing Foundation, University of Southern California

Watch more videos from GitHub Universe 2026: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AArI948SDz8&list=PLENrlAC
title: Sketching with code in the age of AI
